category_zh: 微分方程 / 常微分方程
literal_source_claim_en: Numerical integration of ordinary differential equations.
source_attribution: Carl Runge/Martin Kutta; 1895 (catalog attribution only, not a proposition-level citation)
candidate_family_not_credited_as_stateme: For a source-selected Runge-Kutta tableau and initial-value problem, prove exactly the selected well-definedness, order, error, convergence, stability, or structure-preservation conclusion under its complete assumptions.
statement_blocker: The catalog supplies a method-family name and numerical-integration gloss, not a theorem. It omits the Runge-Kutta tableau and explicit/implicit convention, ODE carrier and domain, vector-field regularity, solution and arithmetic model, step/grid assumptions, and whether the conclusion is a stage identity, consistency/order condition, local or global error, convergence, stability, or invariant-preservation result. Choosing RK4 or any standard theorem would add proposition-changing mathematics and may absorb the separate THM-M-1475 stability target.
domain_and_universes: Open: an exact source must fix autonomous or time-dependent dynamics, scalar, finite-dimensional, or Banach state, time and state scalar fields, vector-field domain, numerical state carrier, grid, norm, and exact or floating-point arithmetic semantics.
conclusion: Open: the repository does not say whether to assert a Runge-Kutta update identity, well-defined stages, consistency/order conditions, local truncation error, global convergence/error, stability, or preservation property.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded at intake because no proposition is selected; every stage, step, interval, domain, solvability, tableau, and uniformity case in scope-map.md must be resolved by the statement phase.
candidate_scope_not_credited: the one-step equations and well-definedness of a fixed explicit or implicit Runge-Kutta tableau
the classical fourth-order method's local truncation or global finite-horizon error under source-specified regularity and Lipschitz assumptions
a necessary-and-sufficient Butcher order-condition theorem for a general finite tableau
finite-horizon convergence of a consistent Runge-Kutta method under a source-selected stability or Lipschitz hypothesis
a source-specific absolute-stability-function or stability-region theorem subject to reconciliation with THM-M-1475
a structure-preservation theorem for a specially constrained Runge-Kutta method
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: zero stages, a degenerate tableau, vanishing weights, and methods whose implicit stage equations have no or multiple solutions
zero, negative, fixed, adaptive, or variable step sizes and a final time not lying on the grid
empty or zero-length intervals, equilibrium and zero vector fields, and numerical evaluations outside the vector-field domain
nonsmooth or non-Lipschitz vector fields and exact solutions that cease to exist before the requested numerical horizon
exact-real versus floating-point arithmetic, roundoff/overflow, and the admissibility of computational certificates
whether local/global error constants are uniform over steps, grids, initial data, and the step-size limit
excluded_substitutions: classical RK4, Euler, midpoint, Heun, Gauss, Radau, or another particular tableau selected without a reviewed source
THM-M-1395 finite differences, THM-M-1397 Adams methods, THM-M-1398 stiff equations, THM-M-1399 backward differentiation formulas, or THM-M-1475 Runge-Kutta stability used as this target
a stage/update definition, generic ODE theorem, Picard iteration, Gronwall estimate, or finite-sum identity presented as the target theorem
a scalar, linear, one-step, fixed-grid, or low-order special case substituted for a broader selected source
a structure or hypothesis that assumes the desired order, error, convergence, stability, or preservation conclusion
a floating-point experiment, simulation, error table, plot, or unchecked symbolic tableau calculation used as theorem evidence
the catalog's untrusted verified label, historical bibliography, API probe, or bounded negative search used as source or proof credit
